item.title: Hours Away From Trump, Xi, Putin Summit in China
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Lori Trahan, a Massachusetts Democrat and co-author of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, discusses Anthropic’s IPO, AI safety rules, tighter chip export controls to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia. Senate Budget Committee Chair Ron Johnson says Republicans will give Democrats another chance to support defense funding before potentially turning to reconciliation, as a December 11 government funding deadline approaches. Former Commerce Secretary and US Ambassador to China Gary Locke discusses expectations for President Trump’s meetings with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, rare-earth supplies, semiconductor export controls and scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fmr. China Amb. Tempers Expectations for Trilat
item.description: Former Commerce Secretary and US Ambassador to China Gary Locke discusses expectations for President Trump’s meetings with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, rare-earth supplies, semiconductor export controls and scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Johnson: Reconciliation Still on the Table
item.description: Senate Budget Committee Chair Ron Johnson says Republicans will give Democrats another chance to support defense funding before potentially turning to reconciliation, as a December 11 government funding deadline approaches. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Milei’s Reform to Suspend Primary Elections Overcomes Key Hurdle
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei’s bill to suspend primary elections next year cleared a senate committee after months on ice, a move he hopes will boost his chances to win re-election against a fragmented opposition.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias

item.description: Rep. Lori Trahan, a Massachusetts Democrat and co-author of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, discusses Anthropic’s IPO, AI safety rules, tighter chip export controls to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Maria Corina Machado Questions Trump Oil Deal While Committing to US Ties
item.description: The US government’s $100 billion deal with a controversial Venezuelan oil baron needs scrutiny, but a long-term partnership with Washington is nevertheless critical for Caracas, said opposition leader María Corina Machado.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Garip and Andreina Itriago

item.title: Senate Permitting Bill Authors Seek Data Center Exemption
item.description: The authors of a sweeping Senate bill to overhaul the federal approval process for major energy projects are proposing an exemption that would allow some data centers to avoid a requirement in the legislation to pay for power-grid upgrades.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: UK Pledges Long-Range Missiles to Ukraine Despite US Criticism
item.description: The UK pledged to send 1,000 long-range cruise missiles to Ukraine, in a pointed signal of British support for strikes deep inside Russia that have been criticized by the US.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: UK to End 1,000-Year-Old Property System With New Law
item.description: A long-awaited law to phase out the 1,000-year-old leasehold system will be put before the UK parliament on Thursday, handing more control to homeowners in the five million properties affected in England and Wales.
item.dc:creator: Meg Short

item.title: Citi CEO Fraser Stresses China Engagement Before Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser emphasized the importance of continued US engagement with China despite intense competition between the world’s two largest economies, as President Donald Trump prepares to meet his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle and Lisa Abramowicz

item.title: Brazil Senate Backs Lula Fiscal Plan as Markets Demand More
item.description: Brazil’s Senate rejected amendments that would have watered down a government plan to curb public spending, a boost for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of his next term in office.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Augusta Saraiva

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Fed Sees More Hikes
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Nearly all Federal Reserve officials agreed in October they would likely have to raise interest rates “in the months ahead” to return inflation to their 2% target in a timely manner. Fed officials last month left interest rates unchanged and reiterated their commitment to containing inflation, but without offering a clear signal on whether they might raise rates at their next meeting in December. Bloomberg’s Mike McKee breaks down the minutes from last months meeting as they roll in.
On today’s episode:
Mike McKee, Bloomberg News International Economics & Policy Correspondent Laura Ullrich, Director of Economic Research at Indeed Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Host Deena Shanker, Bloomberg Businessweek Writer (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Federal Workers Warned Not to Telework for ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
item.description: The Trump administration on Wednesday playfully warned federal workers that the release of the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI does not count as a valid excuse to work from home.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: Jeffries Reelected House Democrat Leader, on Path to Speaker
item.description: Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York was reelected as leader of the House Democrats, putting him on track to become the first Black speaker of the chamber in January. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alaska Shows How Ranked Choice Can Blunt Election Spoilers
item.description: Both the US House and Senate races featured accusations of efforts to confuse voters.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Korte

item.title: Iran Hit Key Infrastructure, Isn’t Behind Outages, US Says
item.description: Trump administration officials said that Iranian cyberattacks have targeted US critical infrastructure and networks since the war began earlier this year, but stressed that recent technology outages and a groundstop of US aircraft were unrelated. Myles Miller has more about what happened on the Hill today (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: More Fed Rate Hates Expected
item.description: Nearly all Federal Reserve officials agreed they would likely have to raise interest rates “in the months ahead” to return inflation to their 2% target in a timely manner. Bloomberg News International Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee. Plus, Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas has been approached regarding the open CEO role at Nvidia. Bloomberg US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King has the story. Then, Indeed Director of Economic Research Laura Ullrich breaks down the 2027 hiring and employment trends. Finally, Bloomberg News Video Game Reporter Jason Schreier reviews the highly anticipated GTA6 releasing in the US at midnight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Says US Envoys to Brief Allies on Trump-Xi-Putin Talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US negotiators will brief allies on Thursday on the outcome of President Donald Trump’s talks in China.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Skolimowski
